subject: Mathematics
chapterName: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates

questions.questionText: What is a coordinate system as defined in the introduction of the chapter?

options.optionText: A structured framework (like grid lines on a map) that uses numbers to describe the exact physical locations of points or objects.
A system used exclusively to measure the temperature and pressure of different geographical regions.
A mathematical tool designed solely for calculating the area of irregular polygons.
A method of organizing historical events in chronological order.

questions.explanationAnswer: According to the text, a system of coordinates is a structured framework (like the grid lines on a map or graph paper) that enables us to use numbers to describe the exact physical locations of points or objects.
questions.explanationQuestion: The question asks for the definition of a coordinate system based on Section 1.1.
questions.correctAnswer: A structured framework (like grid lines on a map) that uses numbers to describe the exact physical locations of points or objects.

questions.questionText: A coordinate system acts as a structured framework that enables us to use numbers to describe the exact physical locations of points or objects.
questions.explanationAnswer: This statement is true as it directly matches the definition of a coordinate system provided in the text.
questions.explanationQuestion: The statement tests the basic definition of a coordinate system.

questions.questionText: A system of coordinates is a structured framework that enables us to use ______ to describe the exact physical ______ of points or objects.
questions.explanationAnswer: The definition states that a coordinate system enables us to use 'numbers' to describe the exact physical 'locations' of points or objects.
questions.explanationQuestion: Fill in the missing key terms from the definition of a coordinate system.

options.optionText: It can be visualized like grid lines on a map or graph paper.
It uses numbers to describe exact physical locations.
It is used only for measuring time intervals.

multi: It can be visualized like grid lines on a map or graph paper.
It uses numbers to describe exact physical locations.
questions.explanationAnswer: The text describes a coordinate system as a structured framework (like grid lines on a map or graph paper) that uses numbers to describe exact physical locations. It is not limited to or used only for measuring time intervals.
questions.explanationQuestion: Identify all correct statements describing a coordinate system based on the text.
questions.questionText: Which of the following statements correctly describe a coordinate system?
Where did the first systematic use of grids occur thousands of years ago on a massive urban scale?
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states: 'The first systematic use of grids occurred thousands of years ago — on a massive urban scale — in the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation.'
questions.explanationQuestion: The question asks for the historical location of the first systematic use of grids on an urban scale.

questions.questionText: In the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation, city streets were constructed with striking precision in North-South and East-West directions at uniform distances of about $100\text{ metres}$ apart.
questions.explanationAnswer: This statement is false. The text states that the streets were constructed at uniform distances of about $10\text{ metres}$ apart, not $100\text{ metres}$.
questions.explanationQuestion: Verify the accuracy of the street spacing dimension mentioned in the text for the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation.

questions.questionText: In the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation, city streets were constructed with striking precision in ______ and ______ directions at uniform distances of about $10\text{ metres}$ apart.
questions.explanationAnswer: The text specifies that the streets were constructed in 'North-South' and 'East-West' directions.
questions.explanationQuestion: Fill in the directions in which the streets of the Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation were aligned.

rightItems: Used East-West and North-South lines for deep geometric constructions (c. 800 C.E.)
First systematic use of grids on a massive urban scale
Formalised the notion and use of zero and negative numbers as algebraic entities
Described the latitudes and longitudes of thousands of locations
questions.explanationAnswer:
Based on the text:
- Sindhu-Sarasvatī Civilisation: First systematic use of grids on a massive urban scale.
- Baudhāyana: Used East-West and North-South lines for deep geometric constructions.
- Ptolemy: Described the latitudes and longitudes of thousands of locations.
- Brahmagupta: Formalised the notion and use of zero and negative numbers.
questions.explanationQuestion: Match each historical entity or mathematician with their respective contribution mentioned in Section 1.1.
questions.questionText: Match the historical figures or civilisations in the left column with their corresponding contributions in the field of mathematics and science in the right column.
Which Greek mathematician (c. $150\text{ BCE}$) described the latitudes and longitudes of thousands of locations, including 'Ozine' (Ujjayinī)?
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states: 'The Greek mathematician Ptolemy (c. $150\text{ BCE}$), building on earlier works including that of Hipparchus, later described the latitudes and longitudes of thousands of locations, including 'Ozine' (Ujjayinī).'
questions.explanationQuestion: Identify the Greek mathematician who mapped thousands of locations using latitudes and longitudes.

questions.questionText: Ptolemy's work on describing latitudes and longitudes built upon earlier works, including that of Hipparchus.
questions.explanationAnswer: This is true. The text explicitly mentions that Ptolemy built on earlier works, 'including that of Hipparchus'.
questions.explanationQuestion: Determine if Ptolemy's work was built upon Hipparchus's earlier contributions.

questions.questionText: The Greek mathematician ______ (c. $150\text{ BCE}$) described the ______ and ______ of thousands of locations, including 'Ozine'.
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states that 'Ptolemy' described the 'latitudes' and 'longitudes' of thousands of locations.
questions.explanationQuestion: Fill in the name of the mathematician and the coordinate terms he described.

questions.questionText: Which ancient location, later identified as Ujjayinī, had its latitude and longitude described by Ptolemy?
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states that Ptolemy described the latitudes and longitudes of thousands of locations, 'including 'Ozine' (Ujjayinī)'.
questions.explanationQuestion: Identify the ancient name used by Ptolemy for Ujjayinī.

questions.questionText: Who formalised the notion and use of zero and negative numbers as algebraic entities, making the four-quadrant Cartesian plane possible?
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states: 'Brahmagupta (c. $628\text{ CE}$) formalised the notion and use of zero and the negative numbers as algebraic entities... Without Brahmagupta's work, the four-quadrant Cartesian plane... would be impossible.'
questions.explanationQuestion: Identify the Indian mathematician responsible for formalising zero and negative numbers as algebraic entities.

questions.questionText: Without Brahmagupta's formalisation of zero and negative numbers, the four-quadrant Cartesian plane would still have been easily developed.
questions.explanationAnswer: This statement is false. The text explicitly states: 'Without Brahmagupta's work, the four-quadrant Cartesian plane, as we will study in this chapter, would be impossible.'
questions.explanationQuestion: Evaluate the necessity of Brahmagupta's work to the development of the Cartesian plane.

questions.questionText: Brahmagupta (c. $628\text{ CE}$) formalised the notion and use of ______ and the ______ numbers as algebraic entities.
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states that Brahmagupta formalised the notion and use of 'zero' and 'negative' numbers.
questions.explanationQuestion: Fill in the mathematical concepts formalised by Brahmagupta.

options.optionText: The 'negative axes' representing values less than zero
The calculation of latitudes using sines

multi: The 'negative axes' representing values less than zero
questions.explanationAnswer: The text states: 'in modern coordinate systems, the 'origin' is zero and the 'negative axes' represent values less than zero. Without Brahmagupta's work, the four-quadrant Cartesian plane... would be impossible.' The calculation of latitudes using sines is associated with Āryabhaṭa, not Brahmagupta's formalisation of zero/negative numbers.
questions.explanationQuestion: Identify all modern coordinate system concepts that directly rely on Brahmagupta's formalisation of zero and negative numbers.
